docs.text: Category: apparel_sarees. Expected weekday-to-weekend revenue ratio: 0.85. Weekday sales are normally about 85% of weekend sales for saree/apparel retailers in tier-2 cities. A ratio below 0.65 for 2+ consecutive weeks indicates an anomaly worth flagging, not seasonal noise. Typical average ticket size: ₹2200. Seasonal peaks: Diwali (Oct-Nov), Wedding season (Nov-Feb), Onam/Pongal regional peaks. Common causes of a weekday dip: New competitor offer nearby, Reduced footfall due to local construction/roadwork, Stock gap in a popular price band, Lapsed repeat-customer outreach.

Category: grocery_kirana. Expected weekday-to-weekend revenue ratio: 0.95. Kirana demand is fairly flat across the week since it serves daily essentials; a >20% single-day drop usually means a stockout of a high-frequency SKU, not demand softness. Typical average ticket size: ₹300. Seasonal peaks: Festival stocking (1-2 weeks before Diwali), Month-start salary cycle (1st-5th). Common causes of a weekday dip: Stockout of a top-selling SKU, Local vendor competition, Price hike on staples.

Category: food_qsr. Expected weekday-to-weekend revenue ratio: 0.8. QSR volumes peak on weekends and evenings; a healthy outlet sees 25-40% of monthly revenue in a compact evening window (7-9pm). Typical average ticket size: ₹260. Seasonal peaks: Exam season (student areas), IPL/cricket season, Monsoon (delivery spike). Common causes of a weekday dip: Delivery platform outage, New nearby competitor, Menu item stockout.

Category: salon_wellness. Expected weekday-to-weekend revenue ratio: 0.55. Salons are heavily weekend and appointment-driven; weekday utilization below 40% of capacity is normal, but a sudden drop in repeat-customer visit frequency is the metric that matters more than daily revenue. Typical average ticket size: ₹900. Seasonal peaks: Wedding season (Nov-Feb), Festive season (Sep-Nov). Common causes of a weekday dip: Staff attrition, Appointment booking friction, Lapsed loyalty outreach.
